children.value: Note that the null hypothesis claims that there is no difference between the means, which can be represented either as “the difference is 0” or as its (algebraically and conceptually) equivalent,

The first way of writing the hypotheses (using a difference between the means) will be easier to use when (in the future) we look for a difference that is not 0.

model.question: What are the appropriate hypotheses for this study?

choices.text: H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0; Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ < 0
choices.feedback: Correct! H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 (no difference); Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ < 0 (smokers' mean length is shorter than non-smokers').

choices.text: H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0; Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ ≠ 0
choices.feedback: The claim is directional (shorter), so the two-sided alternative doesn't capture it.

choices.text: H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0; Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0
choices.feedback: This says smokers' pregnancies are LONGER—the reverse of the claim.

model.hint: The claim being checked is that smokers' pregnancies are SHORTER on average.

model.question: Conceptually, what does the null hypothesis claim in this study?

choices.text: Smoking during pregnancy is not related to pregnancy length
choices.feedback: Correct! H₀ claims smoking status is not related to pregnancy length—the two population means are equal.

choices.text: Smoking during pregnancy shortens pregnancy length
choices.feedback: This is the ALTERNATIVE hypothesis, not the null.

choices.text: The two sample means will be exactly equal
choices.feedback: The null hypothesis concerns the population means, not sample results.

model.hint: Think in terms of the relationship between the two variables.
